title: Level 01
theoryHtml:
Level 01

Graphic design is the process of creating visual content using text, image, colours, shapes and layout to communicate a message clearly and attractively.

Good graphic design organizes information hierarchically and emotionally engages the target audience.

Two type of Graphic :-
  1. Raster graphic — pixel-based images, photographs, and scanned media.
  2. Vector graphic — path-based mathematical curves and scalable graphics.
notice: Study the graphic design principles above, watch the video demonstration, and pass the 5-question assessment to complete this level and unlock the next lesson.

options: Only typing text on a computer

title: Level 02
theoryHtml:
Level 02
1. Raster graphic

Made up of real images (photos) ➔ Call it's pixel

File formats : JPG, PNG, GIF, TIFF

2. Vector graphic

Made up of Vector images (photos/illustrations) ➔ Call it's Path

File formats : SVG, AI, EPS, PDF
notice: Review pixels versus paths, file extensions for both graphic types, and pass the quiz to unlock Level 3.

mcqs.q: What is a Raster graphic made up of?
options: Real images / photos composed of pixels

mcqs.q: Which group contains common file formats for Raster graphics?
What is a Vector graphic constructed of?
options: Call it's Path (mathematical points and vectors)
Fixed pixel grids that blur when resized

mcqs.q: Which group contains standard file formats for Vector graphics?
What happens when you zoom in extensively on a raster image compared to a vector path?
options: Raster stays smooth, Vector becomes pixelated
Raster reveals pixelation/blur, whereas Vector paths stay crisp at any magnification

title: Level 03
theoryHtml:
Level 03

Graphic Design is used to communicate information, Promote products, and create an visual identity.

Main uses of Graphic design :
• Branding (Logos & Brand Identity)
• Advertising (Commercials & Ads)
• Social Media (Posts, Banners & Reels)
• Print Media (Brochures & Books)
• Packaging (Boxes, Pouches & Labels)
• Web & App Design (UI Elements & Icons)
• Marketing (Flyers & Email Campaigns)
• Presentations (Pitch Decks & Slides)
• Entertainment (Posters & Album Covers)
• Information Design (Infographics & Wayfinding)
notice: Study the primary commercial and informational applications of graphic design, then answer the questions to advance.

mcqs.q: What are the three main purposes of Graphic Design?
options: Store data, run calculations, and cool hardware
Communicate information, promote products, and create a visual identity

title: Level 04
theoryHtml:
Level 04
1. Adobe Photoshop
Photo editing & raster graphics

Used for image retouching, digital painting, color grading, and photo manipulation.

2. Adobe Illustrator
Logos, illustrations & vector graphics

The premier vector design tool for scalable logos, iconography, typography, and artwork.

3. CorelDRAW
Vector design, printing & branding

A vector illustration program heavily used in sign-making, vinyl cutting, and print production.

💡 Goal: Install and set up Adobe Illustrator software for vector design lessons.
notice: Study the software tools and their specific domains. Complete the quiz to unlock the Illustrator interface overview.

title: Level 08
theoryHtml:
Level 08

Eyedropper tool is Pick and apply in the color.

Official sampling and application sequence:

1. Create object on the artboard
2. Choose color source (another vector shape, photo, or swatch)
3. Select Eyedropper tool (I)
4. Pick the Choose color by clicking the sample
5. Apply in object directly
notice: Understand how the Eyedropper tool (I) samples color and attributes to apply them to target objects.

mcqs.q: What is the primary function of the Eyedropper tool?

mcqs.q: Can the Eyedropper tool copy stroke weight and transparency alongside color?
options: Yes, it samples appearance attributes including fill, stroke, and transparency

title: Level 09
theoryHtml:
Level 09

Shape builder tool in add (or) divide in shapes.

Practical shape construction sequence:

Step 1: Create shapes that overlap
Step 2: Select shapes together
Step 3: Select shape builder tool (shift + M)
Step 4: Click and drag across regions ➔ Add to Shapes
Step 5: (Press alt) divide / subtract Shapes
Step 6: Apply in tool to finalize combined geometry
notice: Master Shift + M, shape combining, and holding Alt to delete/divide overlapping vector segments.

title: Level 11
theoryHtml:
Level 11

Mastering bezier curves and anchor points:

Straight lines :

Click and release to place anchor points.

Curves lines :

Click and drag to create direction handles bend your path.

Close / End path :

Press escape(ESC) on keyboard (or) Connect to start point.
notice: Study how the Pen tool (P) places anchor points for straight segments and direction handles for curves.

mcqs.q: What is the keyboard shortcut for the Pen tool?

mcqs.q: How do you generate curved lines using the Pen tool?

mcqs.q: What do the direction handles extending from an anchor point control?
options: The angle and curvature (slope) of the path

title: Level 12
theoryHtml:
Level 12

Object and image rotate to 360*

Circular pattern and transformation workflow:

Step 1: Create an object on the artboard
Step 2: Select rotate tool (R)
Step 3: Set 45* point (or desired center reference point)
Step 4: alt + click mouse = Open rotate panel
Step 5: Set angle, click Copy (creates rotated duplicate)
Step 6: Click ctrl + D repeatedly to complete the 360* pattern!
notice: Learn the shortcut R, setting anchor point with Alt+click, and repeating transforms with Ctrl+D.
